summary:
Police in Poland stepped up security around the Constitutional Tribunal on Friday after dozens of protesters gathered to oppose the government's suspension of the court's president, which they say was unlawful. Riot police were locked in a tense standoff with protesters that night, and several people were detained, police said. The government had also suspended two senior justices and moved to bring criminal charges against them.

The Trump administration has approved a potential Patriot missile sale to Ukraine, a move that follows weeks of Kyiv's complaints that its interceptor supplies were dwindling. The value is given as $2.1bn by one account and $3bn by another. Binance suspended trading on its platform after a suspected hack now linked to North Korea, and is attempting to recover $6.3bn stolen, which it describes as complex.

In Ukraine, starving residents of the Russian-held town of Oleshky began evacuating on Friday under a local ceasefire brokered by US first lady Melania Trump, the first joint relief operation of its kind in four years and eight months of war. In Russia, the independent newspaper Novaya Gazeta announced it is ceasing publication after more than three decades, saying it had been killed by state pressure.

headlines.title: Protests and standoff at Poland's Constitutional Tribunal
headlines.summary: Police stepped up security around Poland's Constitutional Tribunal after protesters gathered to oppose the government's suspension of the court's president, which they say was unlawful. Several people were detained after a tense standoff with riot police on Friday night.

headlines.title: US approves Patriot missile sale to Ukraine
headlines.summary: The US has approved a potential Patriot missile sale to Ukraine, valued at $2.1bn by one account and $3bn by another. The approval follows weeks of Ukrainian complaints that its interceptor missile supplies were dwindling.

headlines.title: Binance suspends trading after $6.3bn hack linked to North Korea
headlines.summary: Binance suspended trading on its platform after a suspected hack, now linked to North Korea, that the company describes as complex. It is attempting to recover the $6.3bn stolen, which is believed to be the largest hack of its kind ever.

headlines.title: Residents begin evacuating Oleshky under Russia-Ukraine truce
headlines.summary: Starving residents of the Russian-held town of Oleshky began evacuating on Friday under a local ceasefire brokered by US first lady Melania Trump. An aid convoy of 25 buses arrived with humanitarian aid, and the town has faced food shortages since Russia occupied it in 2022.

headlines.title: Novaya Gazeta to cease publication after Kremlin pressure
headlines.summary: Russia's independent newspaper Novaya Gazeta announced on Friday that it is ceasing publication after more than three decades. The paper said it had been killed by state pressure after years of repression targeting journalists whose reporting was critical of the Kremlin and its Ukraine war.

headlines.title: US, South Korea and Japan reaffirm call for North Korean denuclearisation
headlines.summary: The three countries reaffirmed their commitment to the complete denuclearisation of North Korea on Saturday. Pyongyang continues to reject disarmament, and speculation is mounting over a possible meeting between US President Donald Trump and Kim Jong Un.

headlines.title: Trump reinstates rallies as midterm campaign ends
headlines.summary: Trump reinstated rallies in Kansas and Iowa a day after cancelling them, saying Republicans have a shot in the midterms. A record 47.9 million Americans have already voted in the elections on November 3, which will decide control of Congress.

headlines.title: Train disaster weakens Sánchez ahead of snap election
headlines.summary: A train disaster, the second major rail accident in Spain this year, has put Prime Minister Pedro Sánchez's government's competence on trial. He faces a snap general election in a few weeks and had wanted to campaign on inequality and housing.
